title: [Chapitre] IX et IX bis. [Ateliers] : notes manuscrites (05-15/07/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (from pp. 69-71). E and E' are sets with a symmetric 'disjointness' relation |o|, written ⊥ below. Σ_E is the family of closed subsets of E; Σ*_E probably denotes the same lattice viewed through the (bi)orthogonal closure. supp°_E is the closure of a subset, presumably A ↦ A^⊥⊥. C (also written cosVr°) is the orthogonal-complement operator A ↦ A^⊥, which turns Σ_E into a complete ortholattice-like object.

The data. A correspondence α : E → P(E') induces α_*(S) = supp°_{E'}(ᾱ(S)) on closed sets. Lemma 2 (p. 69) states that the following are equivalent:
- (i) there is a sup-preserving β_* : Σ_{E'} → Σ_E with α_*(S) ⊥ S' ⇔ S ⊥ β_*(S');
- (ii) there is β : E' → P(E) with α(x) ⊥ x' ⇔ x ⊥ β(x');
- (iii) for every x', the set β̄(x') = {x | α(x) ⊥ x'} is closed, i.e. lies in Σ_E.

This page.
- Given (iii), set β_*(x') = C(β̄(x')) = β̄(x')^⊥.
- If β is as in (ii), then β̄(x') = β(x')^⊥. Hence C(β̄(x')) = β(x')^⊥⊥ = closure of β(x'). The two displayed formulas say exactly this: 'closure of β(x') = C(β̄(x'))' and 'C(β(x')) = β̄(x')'. So β_* is the map associated to β, and it is unique.
- Definition: maps α_* satisfying these conditions are called disjunctive correspondences E → E'. β_*, itself a disjunctive correspondence, is the transpose ᵗα_*.
- Scholie: transposition is an involutive bijection Corrdis(E,E') → Corrdis(E',E), with ᵗ(ᵗα_*) = α_*.

Modern reading. These are orthosets (orthogonality spaces) and 'adjointable' relations between them. Condition (α) is the abstract Hilbert-space adjoint ⟨Ax, y⟩ = 0 ⇔ ⟨x, A*y⟩ = 0. Equivalently, α_* is left adjoint to ⊥∘β_*∘⊥ as a Galois connection between the complete lattices of closed sets. Transposition makes the category of orthosets with disjunctive correspondences a dagger (involutive) category. Page 71 goes on to single out 'applications' (maps) as those whose transpose commutes with C, by analogy with finite disjunctions.
errors: No mathematical error is visible. Condition (iii) as stated on p. 69 ('β̄(x') ∈ Σ_E') gives β_* = C∘β̄ only after the sup-extension to arbitrary closed sets, which is left implicit.
The scholie restates involutivity twice: for α_* and for β_* = ᵗα_*. This is redundant but harmless.
On p. 71 Grothendieck himself flags an open question: whether formula (***) for a quasi-disjunctive α_* forces α_* to be a disjunctive correspondence.

ideas.what: Correspondences between sets with orthogonality relations that admit an 'adjoint' β satisfying α(x) ⊥ x' ⇔ x ⊥ β(x')
ideas.modern_name: adjointable maps/relations between orthosets (orthogonality spaces); Galois-adjoint maps between ortholattices
ideas.usually_credited_to: Foulis (Baer *-semigroups, 1960s); Foulis–Randall; Heunen & Jacobs (dagger kernel categories, ~2009-2010); Paseka–Vetterlein (orthogonality spaces, 2020s)

ideas.what: Transposition α_* ↦ ᵗα_* as an involutive bijection Corrdis(E,E') ≅ Corrdis(E',E)
ideas.modern_name: dagger structure on the category of orthosets with adjointable maps
ideas.usually_credited_to: Heunen & Jacobs; Heunen (category of orthosets as a dagger category)

ideas.what: Characterisation of adjointability by closedness of the 'preimage of orthogonality' set β̄(x') = {x | α(x) ⊥ x'}
ideas.modern_name: criterion for adjointability via biorthogonal closure (Galois connection)
ideas.usually_credited_to: standard in Galois-connection / closure-system theory (Birkhoff, Ore)

missed.claim: In 1986 Grothendieck independently sets up what is now the dagger category of orthosets with adjointable relations. He includes the 'abstract adjoint' condition and the involutive transpose, motivated by a theory of 'disjunctions' rather than by quantum logic. The quantum-logic and categorical-quantum-mechanics literature (Foulis, Heunen–Jacobs) does not cite this, and his motivation suggests a different source domain for these structures.
missed.quote: On trouve ainsi une bijection α_* ↦ ᵗα_* : Corrdis(E,E') → Corrdis(E',E)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is relevant to the history of orthogonality spaces and dagger categories. It may show which non-quantum problem (his 'disjunctions') he wanted this formalism for.

missed.claim: Open question noted on p. 71: does the support formula α_*(supp°A) = supp°(ᾱ(A)) for a quasi-disjunctive α_* imply that α_* is a disjunctive correspondence?
missed.quote: J'ignore si la validité de cette formule ... implique que c'est une conv. disjonction
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It is a small, concrete question about adjointability criteria for orthosets that could be settled by a counterexample or a proof.

deep.surprise_reason: The content is a clean but elementary Galois-connection/adjoint construction. It is notable mainly because Grothendieck builds, unprompted, the dagger category of orthosets known from Foulis and Heunen–Jacobs. This is an independent rediscovery rather than a new result.
